channels.title: Alert channels
channels.description: Choose where Vedette sends alerts. With no channel on, alerts only appear in the app.
channels.privacy: Alert content (device names, CVE IDs) leaves the box only to the channels you turn on here and nowhere else. A channel that is off sends no data.
channels.caption: Alert channels
channels.onButFailed: The channel is on, but its last test failed: alerts sent through it may not arrive. Fix the settings and send a test again.
channels.removeBody: Deletes this channel's settings and saved key. Future alerts will not be sent through it.
channels.removed: Channel {{name}} and its saved key were removed.
channels.dialogDesc: Enter the details, save, then send a test to be sure messages arrive.
channels.minSeverityHint: Alerts below this severity are not sent through this channel.
channels.secretSaved: Saved, ending in {{last4}}. Leave empty to keep it.
channels.urlSaved: Saved: {{url}}. The rest of the address is a secret and is not shown. Leave empty to keep it.

err.badUrl: The webhook URL must start with https:// (or http:// on an internal network). Example: https://hooks.company.com/vedette.
err.insecureUrl: Plain http:// is only allowed for hosts on your internal network. Use https:// for this address.
err.blockedUrl: The webhook cannot point at a link-local or multicast address, a cloud metadata service, or an unspecified address.
err.ownUrl: That address is Vedette itself: loopback, Vedette's own container, or one of its ports (8443, 8444, 8765, 514, 6514) on the machine that runs it. For another program on that machine, enter the machine's LAN address and that program's port.
err.shortKey: The signing key needs at least 16 characters. Press Generate random if you want a random one.

channels.needRole: Only administrators can change notification channels.

chat_id.label: Chat ID
chat_id.hint: Number of the chat or group that receives messages. Easiest: type the bot token below, send any message to the bot (or add the bot to a group and post there), then press Find my chat and pick the chat. By hand: open https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates in a browser and read the number in "chat":{"id":…}. Groups usually look like -1001234567890; for a public channel enter @channelname.

secret.label: Bot token
secret.hint: Message @BotFather, send /newbot and paste the token you get (like 123456789:AAH…). The token is the bot's password: share it with nobody. To send to a group, add the bot to the group first.

oa_id.label: OA ID
oa_id.hint: The Official Account ID number, shown in the OA management page or your app in Zalo Developers.

secret.label: Access token (optional)
secret.hint: The current OA access token, if you have one. Leave it empty: Vedette gets one with the refresh token.
secret.hintGrant: Leave it empty: Vedette gets a new access token with the refresh token before the old one ends (about 25 hours).

user_id.label: Recipient ID (user_id)
user_id.hint: The Zalo ID of the person who receives alerts. They must have followed or messaged the OA, and Zalo only lets an OA send consultation messages within about 48 hours of their last interaction. Check the Zalo Developers documentation.

app_id.label: App ID
app_id.hint: The number of your Zalo app, shown in Zalo Developers next to the app name. The app must be linked to the OA.

secret_key.label: Secret key
secret_key.hint: The Secret key of the Zalo app (Zalo Developers, your app, Settings). It stays on the box, encrypted.

refresh_token.label: Refresh token
refresh_token.hint: The OA refresh token from Zalo Developers (API Explorer, OA access token). It lasts about 3 months and works once: Vedette renews the access token by itself every day and keeps the new refresh token it gets back.

zalo.help: Vedette renews the Zalo access token by itself with the refresh token, the App ID and the Secret key, so you set this up once, not every day. Get the OA's refresh token once in Zalo Developers; only if Vedette cannot reach Zalo for about 3 months does it run out, and then you save a new one.
zalo.doc: Zalo's guide to OA access and refresh tokens

provider.label: Provider
provider.hint: Choosing a provider fills in the server, the port and the encryption. You can still change them.

group.password: Mailbox with a password or app password

name.gmail-oauth: Gmail (sign in with your own Google client)

help.gmail: Gmail needs an app password: turn on 2-Step Verification for the Google account, create an app password, and paste it below. The normal Gmail password does not work.
help.yahoo: Yahoo needs an app password: generate one in your Yahoo account under Account security. The username is your full Yahoo address.
help.icloud: iCloud needs an app-specific password, made at account.apple.com under Sign-In and Security. The username is your full iCloud address.
help.zoho: Use your Zoho address and password, or an app-specific password if two-factor sign-in is on. Paid organization domains use smtppro.zoho.com; accounts in another data center use the server shown in Zoho Mail settings.
help.fastmail: Fastmail needs an app password with SMTP access (Settings, Privacy & Security, App passwords). The username is your full Fastmail address.
help.sendgrid: The username is always apikey and the password is an API key with Mail Send permission. Send from a sender or domain verified in SendGrid.
help.mailgun: Use the SMTP credentials of your sending domain (Sending, Domain settings, SMTP credentials), not the API key. Domains in the EU region use smtp.eu.mailgun.org.
help.ses: Use Amazon SES SMTP credentials, not your AWS access keys. Change us-east-1 in the server name to your SES region: the credentials work in that region only.
help.postmark: Paste the Server API token from the server's API Tokens tab. Postmark uses it as both username and password, so there is no username field.
help.brevo: The username is the SMTP login shown in Brevo under SMTP & API, and the password is an SMTP key (not an API key). Send from a domain authenticated in Brevo.
help.microsoft365: Vedette signs in as an app with OAuth2, without a user password. The box also contacts login.microsoftonline.com to get a sign-in token. Your Microsoft 365 administrator does this once:
help.google-workspace: Vedette signs in as a service account with OAuth2, without a user password. The box also contacts oauth2.googleapis.com to get a sign-in token. A Google Workspace super administrator does this once:
help.microsoft365-user: Vedette signs in once as the mailbox's user with a code (no password is stored; Microsoft is ending passwords for SMTP). You need your own app registration; nobody else's client ID is used. The box contacts login.microsoftonline.com for the code and the tokens. Once:
help.outlook: Vedette signs in once as your Outlook.com account with a code, through your own app registration (no password is stored). The box contacts login.microsoftonline.com for the code and the tokens. Once:
help.gmail-oauth: Instead of an app password, sign in once with your own Google OAuth client (Desktop app). Google sends the browser back to http://127.0.0.1, which does not load: you paste that address into Vedette. The box contacts oauth2.googleapis.com to get the tokens. Once:

microsoft365.s1: In Microsoft Entra, register an app. Under API permissions add Office 365 Exchange Online, application permission SMTP.SendAsApp, and grant admin consent.
microsoft365.s2: Under Certificates & secrets create a client secret, and copy its Value.
microsoft365.s3: In Exchange Online PowerShell, register the app: New-ServicePrincipal with the Application ID and the Object ID of the Enterprise application (not of the app registration).
microsoft365.s4: Give it the mailbox: Add-MailboxPermission -Identity <mailbox> -User <service principal ID> -AccessRights FullAccess, and keep SMTP AUTH on for that mailbox.

google-workspace.s1: In the Google Cloud console create a service account, then under Keys add a JSON key and download it.
google-workspace.s2: In the Google Admin console open Security, Access and data control, API controls, Manage Domain Wide Delegation, and add the service account's client ID with the scope https://mail.google.com/.
google-workspace.s3: The mailbox below must be a user of that Google Workspace domain; the service account sends as that user.

microsoft365-user.s1: In the Microsoft Entra admin center open App registrations, New registration. Supported accounts: this organization only (or any organization).
microsoft365-user.s2: Under Authentication, Advanced settings, set Allow public client flows to Yes. The device code sign-in needs it; no redirect URI is needed.
microsoft365-user.s3: Under API permissions add Microsoft Graph, Delegated, SMTP.Send (and keep offline_access). No admin consent is needed unless your tenant asks for it.
microsoft365-user.s4: Copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID into the fields below, and make sure SMTP AUTH is on for the mailbox.
microsoft365-user.s5: Press Sign in with Microsoft, open microsoft.com/devicelogin on any device, enter the code and sign in as the mailbox.

outlook.s1: In the Microsoft Entra admin center (or Azure portal) open App registrations, New registration, with personal Microsoft accounts among the supported accounts.
outlook.s2: Under Authentication, Advanced settings, set Allow public client flows to Yes.
outlook.s3: Under API permissions add Microsoft Graph, Delegated, SMTP.Send.
outlook.s4: Copy the Application (client) ID below, press Sign in with Microsoft, open the address shown, enter the code and sign in with your Outlook.com account.

gmail-oauth.s1: In the Google Cloud console open Google Auth Platform and set it up: Audience External (Internal for a Workspace domain), with your address as a test user.
gmail-oauth.s2: Under Data access add the scope https://mail.google.com/. Then under Audience press Publish app (In production): an app left in Testing loses its sign-ins after 7 days. For your own use, Google shows an unverified-app warning that you can pass.
gmail-oauth.s3: Under Clients create a client of type Desktop app, and copy its client ID and client secret below.
gmail-oauth.s4: Press Sign in with Google, open Google's page, approve. The browser then fails to open http://127.0.0.1:…: copy the whole address from the address bar and paste it here.

host.label: SMTP server
host.hint_oauth: Fixed for this sign-in: Vedette sends the token to the provider's own server only.

port.label: Port
port.hint: 587 for STARTTLS or no encryption, 465 for SSL/TLS. Changing the encryption changes the port to match.

username.label: Username
username.hint_oauth: The mailbox Vedette sends as, for example alerts@company.com. Send from must be this address or one it may send as.
username.hint_mailgun: The SMTP login of the domain, for example postmaster@mg.company.com.
username.hint_ses: The SMTP user name from the SES console, not an AWS access key.
username.hint_brevo: The SMTP login from Brevo, for example 8a1b2c001@smtp-brevo.com.
username.hint_user: Filled in by the sign-in: Vedette sends as the account that signed in.

tenant_id.label: Tenant ID
tenant_id.hint: The Directory (tenant) ID on the app registration's Overview page.
tenant_id.hint_microsoft365-user: The Directory (tenant) ID, your domain, or organizations for any work or school account.

client_id.label: Client ID
client_id.hint: The Application (client) ID on the same page.
client_id.hint_gmail-oauth: The client ID of your Desktop OAuth client, ending with .apps.googleusercontent.com.

from.label: Send from
from.hint: Address shown on the received email.

secret.label: SMTP password
secret.hint: The password of the account on your mail server. Prefer a dedicated account for Vedette.
secret.hint_service: Stays on this box, encrypted. Only the last 4 characters show after saving.
secret.hint_microsoft_oauth: The Value of a client secret of the app registration (not its Secret ID). Client secrets expire: make a new one before then.
secret.hint_google_oauth: Choose the JSON key file you downloaded. It stays on this box, encrypted; Vedette never sends the key itself, only a token request signed with it.
secret.loaded: Key of {{email}} chosen. Save to keep it.
secret.notKey: This file is not a service account key file from Google Cloud.

url.label: Webhook URL
url.hint: The box sends a POST with a JSON body to this address. Use https:// (http:// only on an internal network).

secret.label: Signing key
secret.hint: Each request carries two headers: X-Vedette-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Vedette-Signature (sha256=<hex>). The hex is HMAC-SHA256 with this key over the timestamp, a dot and the raw body (timestamp + "." + body). The receiver recomputes it the same way, compares in constant time and rejects an old timestamp. At least 16 characters.

label.label: Channel label (optional)
label.hint: A name to recognise this channel in the list, for example #it-alerts. It is only shown in Vedette.

secret.label: Incoming Webhook URL
secret.hint: In your Slack app turn on Incoming Webhooks, add it to a channel and paste the URL (starts with https://hooks.slack.com/services/). The URL is a secret: anyone with it can post to that channel.

channel_id.label: Channel ID
channel_id.hint: The channel where approval requests appear, like C04ABCDEF12. In Slack open the channel details and copy the ID at the bottom. Invite the bot to that channel.

app_token.label: App-level token (xapp-…)
app_token.hint: Slack app, Basic Information, App-Level Tokens: create one with the connections:write scope. Used to open the Socket Mode connection.

bot_token.label: Bot token (xoxb-…)
bot_token.hint: Slack app, OAuth & Permissions, after installing the app to your workspace. Needs the chat:write scope.

channels.emailCodes_other: {{count}} users sign in with email codes. They will not be able to sign in until this channel is back on or an administrator resets their two-step sign-in.

quiet.title: Quiet hours
quiet.description: During these hours Vedette holds messages and sends them together when the period ends. Times use the box time zone. Crossing midnight is fine: 22:00 to 06:30 means from evening to the next morning.
quiet.overnight: Quiet from {{from}} this evening until {{to}} the next morning.
quiet.sameDay: Quiet from {{from}} to {{to}} on the same day.

grouping.title: Grouping
grouping.description: Several alerts for the same product within this window become one message. Critical is always sent right away, never held for grouping.
grouping.enabled: Group messages for the same product

approve.title: Approvals
approve.empty: No approvers yet. Add at least one operator or administrator.
approve.noneLeft: Everyone who can approve is already listed
approve.viewers: Viewers cannot be added: only operators and administrators may approve. A response counts only when it comes from a listed address.

hint.slack: Approval requests show Approve and Reject buttons in Slack. This uses Slack Socket Mode: the box opens the connection outward to Slack, so you open no inbound port and need no public address.
hint.telegram: Approval requests show inline Approve and Reject buttons in the chat. This uses the bot above with long polling: the box asks Telegram for new button presses, so you open no inbound port. When you save, the bot sends each approver a confirm link; their presses count once they open it and confirm while signed in to Vedette as themselves.
hint.email: Each approver receives an email with an Approve button that opens a confirmation page on Vedette.
hint.zalo-personal: Add each approver with their Zalo account: pick a friend of this account or find them by phone number. When you save, this account sends each of them a confirm link; they are linked once they open it and confirm while signed in to Vedette as themselves (your own Zalo you confirm here). Then each approval request reaches them privately with two codes of their own, one to approve and one to reject. High-risk actions are approved only in Vedette.

email.p1: The link is single-use, valid for 30 minutes, and bound to that one action and that one approver.
email.p2: The page requires pressing Approve, so mail scanners that only open links cannot approve.
email.p3: The box must be reachable from where the approver opens the email (office LAN or VPN).
email.p4: Replying to the email does not approve anything, because replies are easy to forge.

approve.linkOnly: This channel cannot take approvals. Messages sent here carry a link that opens Vedette, where an operator or administrator approves.

zp.scannedBy: Scanned by {{name}}. Confirm the sign-in on the phone.
zp.scannedConfirm: Scanned. Confirm the sign-in on the phone.

state.declined: The sign-in was declined on the phone.

zp.noRecipient: No recipient yet. Pick a group or a friend, or find one.

zp.signInToPick: Sign in to pick from the account's groups and friends, or find one below.
zp.findLabel: Or find by invite link, phone number or ID
zp.findHint: A group invite link looks like https://zalo.me/g/abcdef123; a phone number like 0912345678.
zp.notMember: The signed-in account is not a member of {{name}}. Join the group with that account in the Zalo app, or alerts will not arrive.

link.unsaved: Save to send this person a confirm link on Zalo (your own Zalo too, unless it is this box's signed-in account: that one you confirm here).
link.waitingFor: Waiting for {{name}} to open the link sent at {{time}} and confirm it while signed in to Vedette.

link.yours: This is the box's own Zalo account, which you signed in with: link it to your Vedette account now.

zp.signOutHint: Zalo has no sign-out for this kind of session: a sign-in you cancel, replace or do not save stays signed in on Zalo until it expires or you log it out of the account's devices in the Zalo app.

incidents.emptyBodyNoTraps: When a machine connects to a known-bad address, a log looks wrong or an unknown device appears, it shows up here and is sent through the channels you turned on.
